# Gareth English (Gareth Montgomery) — Interactive Cambridge C1/C2, IELTS 7.0–8.5 & ESL Teacher Licensing Platform

> Official machine-readable index (`llms.txt`) for `https://garethenglish.com/`. Built by Gareth Montgomery, Cambridge CELTA-qualified educator (2007) with 19 years teaching experience, 15 of them as a Lecturer at Belfast Metropolitan College (specialising in Cambridge B2 First, C1 Advanced, C2 Proficiency, IELTS Academic 7.0–8.5, and Executive Business English).

For full syllabus specifications, feature comparisons, and complete URL mappings, see: [llms-full.txt](https://garethenglish.com/llms-full.txt)

## Original Empirical Classroom & Linguistic Research ("From the Red Pen" 6-Part Series — `https://garethenglish.com/blog.html#research`)
> Open-access empirical classroom research for Cambridge B2/C1/C2 & IELTS candidates, CELTA/DELTA English teachers, and applied linguistics researchers, pairing verified corpus datasets with interactive browser diagnostics:
- **1. The C1/C2 Syntactic Research Lab (189-Sentence Multi-L1 Corpus & L1 Micro-Scrubber)**: Across `N = 189` annotated learner sentences (`3,387` words, `8` anonymised writers across Mandarin, Romance, Slavic, German, and Armenian L1 families), **96.4% (54/56)** of attempted C1/C2 macro-frames are structurally intact (`48/48 = 100%` in full-text scripts), yet pooled raw Error-Free Sentence Ratio (EFSR) sits at **35.4% (67/189)** due to local L1 micro-slips (`OR_MH = 0.943`, `p = 0.8799`). Targeted L1 micro-scrubbing lifts pooled EFSR to **91.0% (172/189, +55.6 pp)** (within-writer mean **32.6% -> 86.2%, +53.6 pp**). Includes an 80-item CPE Part 4 audit (**80.0% [64/80]** nominalisation/idioms/valency, **85.0% [68/80]** requiring a preposition) and a 4-profile L1 Micro-Scrubber: [c1-syntactic-research-lab.html](https://garethenglish.com/c1-syntactic-research-lab.html)
- **2. Cambridge Use of English Under the Microscope (B2 to C2)**: Empirical audit across Part 4 (`N = 92` unique B2/C1/C2 items + `80`-item CPE benchmark), Part 2 Open Cloze (`N = 48` gaps across 6 passages), and Part 3 Word Formation (`N = 40` official sample items + `56` studio stems). Nominalisation, prepositional valency, and fixed idioms climb from **46.7% (7/15)** at B2 to **59.6% (31/52)** at C1 and **84.0% (21/25)** at C2 (**80.0% [64/80]** in the CPE benchmark; `1+1` split bar beside a preposition/particle triples from **16.7%** at B2 to **52.0%** at C2); **91.7% (44/48)** of Part 2 Open Cloze gaps test closed-class grammatical operators (**0.0%** free topical nouns); **79.2% (19/24)** of official C1+C2 Part 3 items require multi-move morphology: [cambridge-use-of-english-research.html](https://garethenglish.com/cambridge-use-of-english-research.html)
- **3. Why Memorised Essay Templates Backfire (Sentence Rhythm & Content-Stripped Skeleton Analysis)**: Across `N = 22` texts (`9` unassisted student drafts, `7` authentic C1/C2 models, `6` formulaic template-stuffed essays), sentence-length SD fails to separate real C1 prose from templates (`6.52w` vs `6.82w`, `d = -0.11`) and raw C1 marker counts invert (`1.57` in real C1/C2 models vs `4.67` in formulaic templates, `d = -1.53`). Closed-class opener variety (`H_opener`, `d = +1.95`, `AUC = 0.976`) and the Syntactic Cadence Quality Score (`SCQS`) separate authentic C1 prose from memorised templates with **100% accuracy (`AUC = 1.000`, `d = +1.83`)**: [why-exam-templates-backfire.html](https://garethenglish.com/why-exam-templates-backfire.html)
- **4. 200 Years of Packing Ideas Into Fewer Words (1818–2026 Diachronic Compression)**: Across `N = 36` texts (`5,296` words: `15` classic 1818–1902 literary passages, `15` paired 2026 C1/C2 transfers, and `6` full modern C1/C2 essays), mean sentence length shrank **30.2%** (`24.97` -> `17.42` words, `p = 0.0020`), semicolon/colon chaining dropped **83.8%**, and finite subordination per sentence dropped **52.6%**, while propositions per sentence held steady (`2.70` -> `2.92`, `p = 0.4778`) via a fivefold (**+407.4%**) rise in nominalisation and participle clauses (+**67.1%** per-100-word idea density): [english-compression-1818-2026.html](https://garethenglish.com/english-compression-1818-2026.html)
- **5. Why C1 Readers Make Basic Slips Out Loud (Spoken vs Written Modality Audit)**: Comparing `N = 62` genuine live spoken slips against `N = 64` untimed written errors (`88` sentences), tense, aspect, and *if-would* conditional slips surge **8.9x** in live speech (**41.9% [26/62]** spoken vs **4.7% [3/64]** written, `p < 0.0001`), whereas articles and uncountable nouns dominate untimed writing (**39.1%** written vs **12.9%** spoken, `p = 0.0011`), alongside a **57.5% (23/40)** target-avoidance rate in unchecked homework sentences: [spoken-vs-written-c1-slips.html](https://garethenglish.com/spoken-vs-written-c1-slips.html)
- **6. Error or Just Style? Why Over-Correcting Hurts Good Exam Essays**: Auditing `N = 98` classroom repairs (**63.3% [62/98]** genuine morphosyntactic errors vs **36.7% [36/98]** grammatical C1 style upgrades) and `N = 45` exam essay sentences across 3 scripts shows that miscounting grammatical phrasing (*discussed if*, *most of the species*) as errors slashes pooled EFSR by **20.0 percentage points** (**51.1% -> 31.1%**, and **60.0% -> 33.3%** [-26.7 pp] in Case Study A): [grammar-error-vs-style-audit.html](https://garethenglish.com/grammar-error-vs-style-audit.html)
